must_remember: In circular polarization, the electric field vector maintains a constant magnitude while its direction rotates continuously in the transverse plane.
The essential conditions for producing circular polarization are two mutually orthogonal linear components with equal amplitudes and a phase difference of $\Delta = (2n + 1)\pi/2$.
A quarter-wave plate introduces a phase retardation of $\pi/2$ (or odd multiples) between ordinary and extraordinary rays, converting linear polarization to circular polarization and vice versa.
Circularly polarized light cannot be distinguished from unpolarized light by a single rotating polarizer because the transmitted intensity remains constant in both cases.
Right-Circularly Polarized (RCP) light corresponds to clockwise rotation, whereas Left-Circularly Polarized (LCP) light corresponds to counter-clockwise rotation when viewed facing the oncoming wave.

glossary.meaning: A polarization state where the electric field vector traces out a circle as a function of time or position, with a constant magnitude.
An optical device made of a birefringent crystal cut parallel to its optic axis, designed to introduce a $\pi/2$ phase shift between orthogonal polarization components.
A mathematical matrix representation used in optics to describe the polarization state of plane electromagnetic waves.
The optical property of a material having a refractive index that depends on the polarization and propagation direction of light (difference between $n_e$ and $n_o$).
The directional sense of rotation of the electric field vector, categorized into Right-Circularly Polarized (RCP) and Left-Circularly Polarized (LCP).
